title: Design System: Domenico Fioravanti — Personal Site

display.purpose: H1-H3, hero name, timeline/explore/next-up titles. Space Grotesk, weight 700, -0.01em tracking.

body.purpose: Profile prose, achievement text, entry summaries. IBM Plex Sans, 1.6 line-height. Anything read as a sentence.

label.purpose: Nav, eyebrows, stats, chips, tags, meta lines, status bar, footer. JetBrains Mono, uppercase, letter-spaced. Anything that reads as system chrome or CLI output.

motion.name: cursor-blink
motion.purpose: The hero tagline's terminal cursor block — the system's one recurring motion signature.

motion.name: theme-transition
motion.purpose: Smooths the dark/light mode toggle so the swap doesn't flash.

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Shell-path-styled nav item: '~/' prefix, mono, lowercase; amber when active.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { text-decoration: none; color: #8b93a1; font-size: 0.9rem; font-weight: 500; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; text-transform: lowercase; } .ds-nav-link::before { content: '~/'; opacity: 0.55; } .ds-nav-link[aria-current='page'] { color: #ffb454; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: #ffb454; }

components.name: Mode Toggle Button
components.description: Bordered icon+label button that switches dark/light mode; border turns amber on hover.
components.css: .ds-mode-toggle { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.8rem; background: #12161d; color: #eef0f3; border: 1px solid #242a34; border-radius: 2px; padding: 0.35rem 0.6rem; cursor: pointer; line-height: 1; transition: border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-mode-toggle:hover, .ds-mode-toggle:focus-visible { border-color: #ffb454; outline: none; }

components.name: CLI Flag Chip
components.description: Focus-area tag styled as a command-line flag ('--org-design') rather than a generic pill.
components.css: .ds-chip { border: 1px solid #242a34; border-radius: 2px; padding: 0.35rem 0.75rem; font-size: 0.85rem; background: #12161d; color: #eef0f3; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; list-style: none; display: inline-flex; } .ds-chip::before { content: '--'; opacity: 0.5; margin-right: 0.1em; }

components.name: Bordered Grid Cell
components.description: The recurring stat/explore/stack-matrix cell: flush-bordered, no radius, 1px hairline gaps between siblings act as the divider.
components.css: .ds-grid-cell { background: #12161d; padding: 1.1rem 1.2rem; } .ds-grid-value { display: block; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 1.6rem; font-weight: 600; color: #ffb454; } .ds-grid-label { display: block; margin-top: 0.35rem; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.7rem; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8b93a1; }

components.name: Bracket Section Heading
components.description: Auto-numbered CLI-output-style section label, e.g. '[ 01 profile ]'. Number increments via a shared CSS counter across the page.
components.css: .ds-section-heading { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8b93a1; display: block; margin-bottom: 0.75rem; } .ds-section-heading::before { content: '[ 01 '; color: #8b93a1; } .ds-section-heading::after { content: ' ]'; color: #8b93a1; }

components.name: Command-Output List Item
components.description: Achievement row prefixed with a green 'ok' marker, reading as passing test/log output.
components.html: • okBuilt engineering orgs from scratch to 45+ people
components.css: .ds-log-item { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 2.25rem 1fr; gap: 1rem; padding: 0.9rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #242a34; list-style: none; } .ds-log-ok { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; color: #4ade80; font-size: 0.85rem; }

components.name: Git-Log Timeline Row
components.description: Career-history row styled as a git-log graph node: filled amber dot + 'HEAD' badge for the current role, hollow dot otherwise, connected by a vertical hairline.
components.html:
Senior Director of EngineeringHEAD

2023-02 → present
components.css: .ds-timeline-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 16px 1fr; column-gap: 1.75rem; } .ds-timeline-marker { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; } .ds-timeline-dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; margin-top: 6px; background: #242a34; border: 1px solid #8b93a1; } .ds-timeline-dot--current { background: #ffb454; border: none; } .ds-timeline-line { width: 1px; flex: 1; margin-top: 6px; background: #242a34; } .ds-timeline-title { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 1.15rem; font-weight: 600; color: #eef0f3; } .ds-head-badge { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.7rem; color: #0b0e13; background: #ffb454; padding: 0.15rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 2px; } .ds-timeline-when { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.8rem; color: #8b93a1; margin: 0 0 0.85rem; }

narrative.overview:
The site presents itself as a live terminal session rather than a document. The wordmark reads as a login prompt (domenico@fioravanti), navigation links wear a ~/ path prefix like shell aliases, section headings are auto-numbered CLI output ([ 01 profile ]), the hero tagline is typed after a > prompt marker with a genuine blinking cursor, and the résumé's proudest facts render as command output: a green ok status per achievement, a git log --roles timeline for the career history, a stack --list matrix for technology depth. Nothing here is illustrative or decorative — every visual device is a real piece of developer-tool vocabulary, chosen because the audience (engineering hiring managers) reads that vocabulary fluently and it doubles as a credibility signal.

The system rejects conventional résumé/portfolio warmth (soft shadows, rounded cards, editorial serif type, generous whitespace-as-luxury) in favor of the flat, dense, monospace-inflected register of an IDE or terminal emulator. It is confident and technical rather than approachable and personal — the persona is a senior engineer's own tool, not a marketing site about one.
keyCharacteristics: Full dark/light mode pair, dark-first (a terminal's native state), both built from the same four-tier neutral system (bg → bg-panel → bg-panel-2 → fg).
A single functional accent (Terminal Amber) plus one narrowly-scoped status color (Log-Success Green) — never more than two colors doing work on screen at once.
Zero shadows anywhere; depth comes from background-tier shifts and hairline borders only.
Near-flat geometry (2px radius) — corners are barely softened, not rounded.

Monospace (JetBrains Mono) carries all metadata, labels, and system chrome; a geometric sans display face (Space Grotesk) carries headings and titles; a humanist sans (IBM Plex Sans) carries body prose. Three faces, three distinct jobs, never mixed within one role.

rules.name: The Two-Color Rule
rules.body: Only Terminal Amber and Log-Success Green ever carry semantic color; everything else is neutral. A third color anywhere is a bug, not a variant.

rules.name: The Status-Color Rule
rules.body: Log-Success Green appears in exactly two places: the live status-bar dot and the achievements list's ok marker. It signals 'this ran successfully,' never decoration, never a second accent.

rules.name: The Prose-Is-Sans Rule
rules.body: The moment text is read as a sentence rather than scanned as a label or datum, it drops out of mono into IBM Plex Sans. Mono marks 'this is system output,' never paragraphs.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a box-shadow, blur, or glow. If something needs to look 'raised,' give it a border and a panel-tier background shift instead — the same tool a terminal or IDE would use.

dos: Do keep every UI-chrome label (nav, eyebrows, stats, tags, meta lines) in JetBrains Mono; reserve IBM Plex Sans strictly for read-as-prose text.
Do express new "signature" content (a new résumé section, a new list) as a piece of real developer/terminal vocabulary (a log, a diff, a status line, a manifest) rather than a generic card or hero.
Do keep the bordered-grid pattern (1px outer border, 1px hairline-filled gaps) as the default for any new multi-item grouping.
Do hold the accent to Terminal Amber only; if a second signal color is ever needed, it must be as narrowly scoped as Log-Success Green currently is.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow, glow, or blur anywhere — depth is background-tier and border only.
Don't round any corner beyond 2px, and don't round outer panel/grid containers at all.
Don't introduce a third brand color, a gradient, or a decorative illustration — the system's restraint (near-monochrome + one accent) is load-bearing, not incidental.
Don't widen the reading column past its current narrow, single-track feel to chase a "landing page" width; the site is designed to be read closely, not scanned broadly.
Don't invent warmth-signaling devices (soft serif display type, generous rounded cards, editorial photography treatment) — that's a different, explicitly-rejected register for this audience.
